provider_readback.text:
A trapped ant. A hidden thread. Its colony-mates targeted the restraint.

In laboratory trials with Cataglyphis cursor, workers dug sand, pulled at an active nestmate’s limbs and sometimes bit the nylon snare holding it. Rescue behaviour appeared in all 9 group tests with active colony-mates, but none of the 45 tests involving other stimuli or controls. Each test had five potential rescuers; only one to three helped in positive tests.

These counts describe groups of ants in a controlled artificial setup, not the percentage of individual ants that help. The study did not establish that every ant escaped, why the response was triggered, that ants felt empathy, or how often this happens in nature.

Nowbahari et al. (2009), PLOS ONE 4:e6573. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0006573
Open paper: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2719796/
Research record: https://akshaymohan16.github.io/toxic-tales-library/sources/tt-009.html
